query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: seat_comfort_issue
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of dissatisfaction; a service attribute whose effect on rating/recommendation is being attributed.

per_column.name: food_quality_decline
per_column.rationale: Candidate service-quality cause of low ratings.

per_column.name: service_inconsistency
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause affecting satisfaction and recommendation.

per_column.name: customer_service_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause; responsiveness plausibly drives the outcome.

per_column.name: booking_operational_failure
per_column.rationale: Candidate operational cause of poor experience and low rating.

per_column.name: aircraft_age_condition
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause affecting comfort/experience and rating.

per_column.name: traveller_segment
per_column.rationale: Traveller type plausibly affects both which service issues are experienced/expected (treatment) and baseline rating tendencies (outcome). Present in original data as Type of Traveller but re-surfaced as an adjustment variable; not named in query.

per_column.name: cabin_class
per_column.rationale: Cabin class plausibly affects service/comfort levels received (treatment) and satisfaction expectations/ratings (outcome), making it a common cause. Not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The added columns clearly supply candidate TREATMENTS (multiple service-quality/operational causes) whose effect on the outcome is being attributed. Two columns (traveller_segment, cabin_class) function as plausible confounders -- common causes of both the service experience received and the rating given -- and neither is named in the query, so they show some genuine causal reasoning. However, they overlap heavily with existing original columns (Type of Traveller, Class), so they are re-encodings rather than newly surfaced latent confounders, and one could argue class partly lies on the causal path. The confounder set is thin (only two, both plausibility ~0.6) relative to many treatments, and several treatments themselves risk being mediators of one another. Overall the causal setup is partially realised: treatments present, confounders present but modest in quality and originality.
